title: Multiplying and Dividing Fractions and Mixed Numbers
seo_title: Year 7 Multiplying and Dividing Fractions Worksheets: Fractions of Amounts, Reciprocals and Keep Change Flip
standard_text: Use the four operations, including formal written methods, applied to integers, decimals, proper and improper fractions, and mixed numbers, all both positive and negative; use reciprocals.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 worksheets on multiplying and dividing fractions: fractions of amounts, multiplying fractions and mixed numbers, reciprocals, keep-change-flip division and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply: tops × tops, bottoms × bottoms. Divide: keep, change, flip.
key_sub: Change mixed numbers to improper fractions first, and simplify your answer.
body_html:
How it works

Multiplying: multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators, then simplify. “Of” means multiply: 2/3 of 12 = 2/3 × 12 = 8.

Dividing: keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip the second fraction (use its reciprocal).

Change mixed numbers into improper fractions before you multiply or divide.

Example

Work out 3/4 × 2/5.

3 × 2 = 6 and 4 × 5 = 20.

6/20 simplifies to 3/10.

Answer: 3/10

Example

Work out 2/3 ÷ 4/9.

Keep, change, flip: 2/3 × 9/4.

= 18/12 = 3/2.

Answer: 1 1/2

Example

Work out 1 1/2 × 2 2/3.

Improper: 3/2 × 8/3 = 24/6.

Answer: 4

Common mistakes

  • Multiplying the denominator by a whole number: 2/5 × 3 = 6/5, not 6/15.
  • Flipping the first fraction instead of the second when dividing.
  • Multiplying mixed numbers in parts: 1 1/2 × 2 2/3 is not 2 2/6.
  • Thinking the answer to a division must be smaller: 6 ÷ 3/4 = 8.

faq.a: Multiply the numerators, multiply the denominators, then simplify. You do not need a common denominator.
Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip the second fraction. 2/3 ÷ 4/9 = 2/3 × 9/4 = 3/2.
The number you multiply by to get 1. The reciprocal of 3/5 is 5/3, and the reciprocal of 4 is 1/4.

faq.q: Why can dividing by a fraction give a bigger answer?
faq.a: Because you are asking how many small pieces fit in. 6 ÷ 3/4 = 8 pieces of three quarters.

A ribbon is 6 m long. How many pieces of 34 m can be cut from it?
items.e: 6 ÷ 34 = 6 × 43 = 8.

items.q: A ribbon is 5 m long. How many pieces of 13 m can be cut from it?
items.e: 5 ÷ 13 = 5 × 31 = 15.

items.q: A ribbon is 4 12 m long. How many pieces of 34 m can be cut from it?
items.e: 4 12 ÷ 34 = 92 × 43 = 6.

items.q: A ribbon is 10 m long. How many pieces of 25 m can be cut from it?
items.e: 10 ÷ 25 = 10 × 52 = 25.

items.q: A field is 34 of a farm. 23 of the field is planted with wheat. What fraction of the farm is wheat?
items.e: “Of” means multiply: 34 × 23 = 12.

items.q: 25 of a class are girls. 12 of the girls play netball. What fraction of the class are girls who play netball?
items.e: “Of” means multiply: 25 × 12 = 15.

items.q: A jug is 56 full of juice. 35 of the juice is poured out. What fraction of the jug was poured out?
items.e: “Of” means multiply: 56 × 35 = 12.

items.q: A rectangle measures 2 12 m by 1 13 m. What is its area?
items.e: Area = 2 12 × 1 13 = 52 × 43 = 3 13 m².

items.q: A rectangle measures 1 34 m by 23 m. What is its area?
items.e: Area = 1 34 × 23 = 74 × 23 = 1 16 m².

items.q: A rectangle measures 2 14 m by 3 13 m. What is its area?
items.e: Area = 2 14 × 3 13 = 94 × 103 = 7 12 m².

items.q: A bottle holds 34 of a litre. How many bottles can be filled from 12 litres?
items.e: 12 ÷ 34 = 12 × 43 = 16.

items.q: A music lesson lasts 14 of an hour. How many lessons fit into 3 hours?
items.e: 3 ÷ 14 = 3 × 41 = 12.

items.q: Each glass holds 56 of a pint. How many glasses can be filled from 2 12 pints?
items.e: 2 12 ÷ 56 = 52 × 65 = 3.

items.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 1 23 cups of flour. How much flour is needed for 2 people?
items.e: Half of 1 23 = 53 × 12 = 56 cups.

items.q: A cake is cut so that 34 of it is left. It is shared equally between 6 people. What fraction of the whole cake does each person get?
items.e: 34 ÷ 6 = 34 × 16 = 18.

items.q: 23 of a pizza is shared equally between 4 friends. What fraction of the pizza does each friend get?
items.e: 23 ÷ 4 = 23 × 14 = 16.
